title: Choose the dashboard look
question: Which look should the Habit Tracker dashboard take? The seed-packet direction leads. You can take the blister strip, the familiar habit-app standard, or ask for a fresh set.

options.label: Seed Packet
options.lineage: Commercial seed packets, read as a working screen
options.thesis: Each habit is a named crop, and the week is a sowing row you fill by marking it done.
options.viewport: A yellow bar holds the name and theme switch. Under it, this week's totals. Three habit rows sit on a light field: the name on the left, a sowing row and Mark Done locked to one rail on the right. Green appears only as the Completed badge when a row is full.
options.risk: If the plant language gets louder than the check-off, it starts to feel like a garden catalog.

raised.raise: The sowing row is the only progress graphic, drawn in full indigo, not a grey track with a tint.
The habit you just marked is the loudest row. The others stay quiet.
Green is reserved for the Completed badge and is never used as decoration.
Every week row shares one size and one baseline, so 4/7 and 3/5 compare by eye.
The week rows are the display-scale signal. Names and secondary actions stay smaller.
Names sit left. The week row and Mark Done share one vertical rail.

options.label: Blister Strip
options.lineage: A weekly blister card you punch as you go
options.thesis: The week is a strip of cells. Mark Done punches the next open cell.
options.viewport: A green header rail, then the week totals, then three cards. Each card's week is a row of cells: filled, open, or stamped Completed. Mark Done sits on the same rail as the next open cell.
options.risk: This is the familiar row of dots most habit apps already ship.

options.label: Transit Diagram
options.thesis: Habits would be colored lines, and the week would be stations along a route.
options.viewport: A route map of three short lines, with Mark Done as a transfer.
options.case: A rail map is a journey, not a check-off. The home scene does not read as a station.
options.kept: The week row is the only progress graphic, drawn at full strength.
options.risk: The screen becomes a map costume and the check-off gets lost.

options.label: Streaming Wall
options.thesis: Each habit would be a tile that grows when you land on it.
options.viewport: Horizontal rows of habit posters, details hidden until focus.
options.case: You have three habits to mark, not a catalog to browse. Hiding the week count makes you hunt.
options.kept: The habit you just marked becomes the loudest row.
options.risk: Progress stays hidden until a tile is focused.

options.label: Orienteering Map
options.lineage: A course in purple over forest terrain
options.thesis: Marking a habit would punch the next control on a map.
options.viewport: A terrain map with three purple controls and a legend.
options.case: The weekly count is not a route through terrain, and the sample habits are not a course.
options.kept: Green is reserved for the Completed badge and nothing else.
options.risk: A map legend replaces the list you need to scan.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.lineage: Five plates of one plant, seed to husk
options.thesis: A habit would move through life stages on matching plates.
options.viewport: Five equal plates for each habit, labeled seed through husk.
options.case: The product has a weekly count, not life stages. The plates would invent a progress model it does not have.
options.kept: Every week row shares one size and one baseline.
options.risk: Cream paper and a serif make it the default garden app.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Habit names would become color codes on a black field.
options.viewport: A black field, a pulse of white lines, and a color strip in place of the habit name.
options.case: Hiding the habit name fails the check-off. A nightclub sleeve is not this person's morning.
options.kept: The week rows are the display-scale signal. Everything else stays small.
options.risk: Black and neon is a costume, and the green badge loses its meaning.

options.label: Emission Rail
options.lineage: A charcoal spectrogram on a viewing box
options.thesis: Progress would be hairline marks whose height carries the state.
options.viewport: A dark plate of thin colored lines, one rail, no filled week.
options.case: Hairlines fail a glance at 4 of 7, and a lab instrument is not the home check-off.
options.kept: Names sit left. The week and Mark Done share one vertical rail.
options.risk: State disappears into lines too thin to read.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.lineage: The soft habit app most people already know
canonCard.thesis: Rounded cards in a column, a thin progress bar, and a quiet header.
canonCard.viewport: A plain header, then stacked cards. The week is a thin bar under the name, and Mark Done is a green button.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other habit app, on purpose.
